reasoning: Both the problem and the specific empirical approach are already published. At the problem level, the "foundation model monoculture / single point of failure" framing — that models sharing a base inherit correlated safety failures — is established in Bommasani et al.'s "On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models" and "Picking on the Same Person" (outcome homogenization from shared components). At the method level, Angell et al.'s "Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations" / "Jailbreak Strength and Model Similarity Predict Transferability" (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2506.12913) does almost exactly the proposed study but larger and deeper: 20 open-weight models x 33 jailbreaks, computing pairwise transfer/correlation, explicitly distinguishing within-family vs cross-family pairs, and showing representational similarity (driven by shared base) predicts shared failures. "One Leak Away" (arXiv 2512.14751) separately confirms fine-tuned variants inherit base-model jailbreak vulnerabilities. The proposed phi/Jaccard correlation matrix on ~60 items and 6-8 models is a methodologically simpler subset of this existing work, offering no clear unexplored angle.

evidence.title: Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations (Jailbreak Strength and Model Similarity Predict Transferability)
evidence.summary: Across 20 open-weight models and 33 jailbreak attacks, shows pairwise representational similarity predicts symmetric jailbreak transfer AUROC, explicitly plots within-family vs cross-family model pairs, and demonstrates that increasing similarity (incl. shared base) increases shared/correlated failures. Directly covers the proposed within-base vs cross-family failure-correlation study at larger scale.

evidence.title: One Leak Away: How Pretrained Model Exposure Amplifies Jailbreak Risks in Finetuned LLMs
evidence.summary: Empirically shows jailbreak prompts against a source pretrained LLM transfer most effectively to its finetuned variants, i.e. finetuned models inherit base-model vulnerabilities — the core 'shared base => correlated failure' claim of the proposal.

evidence.title: On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models
evidence.summary: Establishes the conceptual problem: a foundation model adapted to many applications is a single point of failure, with correlated safety/security failures and homogenization propagating across all derivatives — the 'concentration risk' the proposal aims to map.

evidence.title: Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture lead to Outcome Homogenization?
evidence.summary: Bommasani et al. formalize and empirically measure outcome homogenization (systematically correlated failures on the same individuals) from systems sharing components such as training data or pretrained base models, including foundation-model settings.

evidence.title: Simulated Ensemble Attack: Transferring Jailbreaks Across Fine-tuned Vision-Language Models
evidence.summary: Reports >86.5% jailbreak transfer success across diverse fine-tuned variants sharing a base, reliably exploiting inherited base-model vulnerabilities — further confirming high within-base failure correlation.
